spec_notes: R-1 decides in an ordinary requirement line that malformed FEN behaviour is outside the contract, without marking it as the builder's assumption (the request is silent). spec.md does not state castling's out-of/through/into-check rules (S-22..S-24) or the king-two-square UCI form (S-25); these appear only in architecture.md AD-1 and the tests. R-4 pins Kiwipete as 'the middlegame position' for the 50 ms limit, a choice a correct product need not share. R-4 says 'Verify ... package manifest' but no test checks the manifest or dependencies. No contradiction of the request found.
tests_notes: Several tests bundle many behaviours (TC-1 'rejects malformed moves, wrong turns, blocked pieces and pins'; TC-1 fields test covers turn, ep, both clocks and BigInt clocks; castling-rejection test covers six cases in a loop). assert.throws(fn, IllegalMoveError) silently degrades to 'throws anything' if the export is missing: removing IllegalMoveError from module.exports leaves all 12 tests passing. TC-3 is timing-based (generous margins; Kiwipete measured once, cold). Tests that would fail on another correct build: TC-1 asserts 'E2E4' and 'e2e4\n' are rejected (the inventory allows a documented build to accept other case or trim whitespace), and asserts exact clocks at 9007199254740992+1, which a correct Number-based build cannot represent. No test reaches internals or file names beyond src/chess. No invalid-FEN test.
maintainer: The 0x88 board and readFen's lack of validation mean any parsing change (e.g. adding FEN validation) touches index arithmetic that silently tolerates garbage today, so behaviour on bad input could shift unpredictably. Castling safety is split between castleMoves (start and transit squares) and the general king-safety filter (destination), and castling rights depend on the ROOK_RIGHTS index map; changing either without noticing the other could reopen castling-through-check bugs, though the castling tests would catch the common cases.
